answer: Trust is forged from a single stake: before an agent can trade, it locks a refundable deposit and publishes one signed attestation. Peers then view every identity through a shared prism of stake, timing, and behavior, so a lone actor cannot hide a swarm of fakes behind one face. Reputation grows like a vine: each honest trade extends the chain of attestations, and a bad act severs it. If the same attestation appears under two names, both deposits are slashed and both identities frozen. An attacker must buy a new proof and stake for every fake, while an honest agent pays once and keeps trading.
